gap: No result ChatGPT got gives today's prices for the whole built-in-preamp range: the Sony PS-LX3BT is $398.00 at World Wide Stereo, not the $349.99 on ChatGPT's card or the $348 Platter & Plinth quotes, and the AT-LP120XUSB is $399.00, not the $349 Valve & Vinyl and Platter & Plinth list. That makes the Fluance RT81 ($299.99) about $100 cheaper than either and the AT-LP70X ($249, Black/Bronze only) the cheapest switchable-preamp deck that ChatGPT's answers named.
standout_why: I compared against Valve & Vinyl (crosley-alternatives, priced Nov 9), Platter & Plinth (best-with-preamp, priced Nov 9), TheBrickFantastic (no prices, only 'under $300' style figures) and FewBetter (the URL now serves an earbuds page with no turntables). Valve & Vinyl and Platter & Plinth already price the AT-LP70X ($249), RT81 ($299.99), LP60X ($179) and LP60XBT ($279), so most of this range is already priced there. What they lack is today's drift (LP120XUSB back to $399 from their $349; PS-LX3BT at $398 against their $348), the color price split on the AT-LP70X and LP70XBT ($249 vs $269; $299 vs $319), and the RT81+ price ($349.99) next to the RT82 at the same $349.99 with no preamp. Neither page gives the RT81's line output level (Platter & Plinth says 'Preamp output: None stated for any deck').
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's pick order on price. AT-LP70X at $249 (Black/Bronze) is the cheapest automatic deck ChatGPT named with a switchable preamp and an upgradeable VM95 stylus. The AT-LP60X at $179 is cheaper but needs a stylus-swap trade-off (ATN3600L, conical, per Platter & Plinth). Fluance RT81 at $299.99 is the manual pick. The PS-LX3BT and LP120XUSB both cost about $100 more than the RT81 today, not the $50 ChatGPT's cards implied, which weakens the Sony card ('Bluetooth convenience') against the AT-LP70XBT at $299. The AT-LP70XBT gives Bluetooth plus a switchable preamp for $99 less.
